title: Polygons and Quadrilaterals: Angle Sums and Parallelograms
seo_title: Polygons and Quadrilaterals Worksheet: Parallelograms, Rhombus, Trapezoid (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on polygons and quadrilaterals: interior and exterior angle sums, parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, trapezoids and kites. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Interior angles of an n-gon add to (n − 2) × 180°. Exterior angles add to 360°.
key_sub: Parallelograms: opposite sides and angles congruent, diagonals bisect each other.
body_html:
How it works

The interior angles of a polygon with n sides add to (n − 2) × 180°. The exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°.

A parallelogram has opposite sides parallel and congruent, opposite angles congruent, consecutive angles supplementary, and diagonals that bisect each other.

  • Rectangle: a parallelogram with four right angles; its diagonals are congruent.
  • Rhombus: a parallelogram with four congruent sides; its diagonals are perpendicular and bisect its angles.
  • Square: both a rectangle and a rhombus.
  • Trapezoid: exactly one pair of parallel sides; its midsegment is the average of the bases. An isosceles trapezoid has congruent base angles.
  • Kite: two pairs of consecutive congruent sides; its diagonals are perpendicular.
Example

Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 144°. How many sides?

Exterior angle: 180 − 144 = 36°

360 ÷ 36 = 10

Answer: 10 sides

Example

ABCD is a parallelogram with m∠A = (3x + 10)° and m∠B = (2x + 20)°. Find m∠A.

Consecutive angles add to 180: 5x + 30 = 180

x = 30, so m∠A = 100°

Answer: 100°

Common mistakes

  • Using n × 180° for the angle sum. Subtract 2 first.
  • Setting consecutive angles of a parallelogram equal. They add to 180°.
  • Saying every parallelogram has congruent diagonals. Only rectangles do.
  • For a trapezoid midsegment, averaging the legs instead of the bases.

faq.q: What is the formula for the sum of the interior angles of a polygon?
faq.a: (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides.

faq.q: What are the properties of a parallelogram?
faq.a: Opposite sides are parallel and congruent, opposite angles are congruent, consecutive angles are supplementary, and the diagonals bisect each other.
Yes. A square has four congruent sides, so it is a rhombus. It is also a rectangle.

faq.q: How do you find the midsegment of a trapezoid?
faq.a: Add the lengths of the two bases and divide by 2.

ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = x + 15 and CD = 2x + 11. Find AB.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: x + 15 = 2x + 11, so x = 4. AB = 19.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = 5x − 6 and EC = 3x + 14. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: 5x − 6 = 3x + 14, so 2x = 20 and x = 10. AC = 2 × 44 = 88.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 6x − 2 and CD = 2x + 26. Find AB.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: 6x − 2 = 2x + 26, so 4x = 28 and x = 7. AB = 40.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = 2x + 6 and EC = x + 12. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: 2x + 6 = x + 12, so x = 6. AC = 2 × 18 = 36.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 3x + 13 and CD = 4x + 8. Find AB.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE = 6x + 12 and ED = 5x + 17. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so BE = ED: 6x + 12 = 5x + 17, so x = 5.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. m∠A = (5x + 6)° and m∠B = (3x + 14)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠A and ∠B are consecutive angles, so they are supplementary: (5x + 6) + (3x + 14) = 180, 8x = 160, x = 20.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 2x and BD = 6x − 16. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: 6x − 16 = 2(2x), x = 8.

items.q: A rhombus has one side of length 5. What is its perimeter?

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 6. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 12 and m∠AEB = 90°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = x + 8 and BD = 5x − 11. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: 5x − 11 = 2(x + 8), x = 9.

items.q: Find the length of the midsegment of the trapezoid.
items.e: The midsegment of a trapezoid is the average of the bases: (12 + 15) ÷ 2 = 13.5.

items.q: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. m∠A = 111° and m∠C = 33°. Find m∠B.
items.e: In a kite, the angles between the pairs of unequal sides (∠B and ∠D) are congruent. 2 × m∠B = 360 − 111 − 33 = 216, so m∠B = 108°.

items.q: In isosceles trapezoid ABCD, the bases are AB and CD, and m∠A = 54°. Find m∠B.

items.q: A parallelogram has one right angle. What must it be?
items.e: Consecutive angles are supplementary and opposite angles are equal, so all four angles are 90°. A rectangle.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 6x + 3, CD = 5x + 13, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 6x + 3 = 5x + 13, so x = 10.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 5x + 8, CD = 2x + 23, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 5x + 8 = 2x + 23, so 3x = 15 and x = 5.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 4x + 1, CD = 3x + 9, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 4x + 1 = 3x + 9, so x = 8.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has perpendicular diagonals?
items.e: Rhombuses (including squares) and kites have perpendicular diagonals. Rhombus.

items.q: Is every rhombus a square?
c: Only if it is a trapezoid
items.e: A rhombus is a square only if it has right angles. No, only sometimes.

items.q: Which property does a rhombus have that a general parallelogram does not?
items.e: Every parallelogram has the other three properties. Its diagonals bisect its angles.

items.q: Which fact is enough to prove ABCD is a parallelogram?
c: Two pairs of consecutive sides are congruent
One pair of opposite sides is parallel
One pair of opposite sides is both parallel and congruent
items.e: One pair of opposite sides that is both parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. One pair of opposite sides is both parallel and congruent.

items.q: Is every square a rhombus?
c: Only if its diagonals are not equal
items.e: A square has four congruent sides, which is the definition of a rhombus. Yes, always.

items.q: Is a rectangle a parallelogram?
c: Only if it is a square
items.e: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides. Yes, always.

items.q: A parallelogram has perpendicular diagonals. What must it be?
items.e: A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. A rhombus.

items.q: A parallelogram has congruent diagonals. What must it be?
items.e: A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle. A rectangle.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are congruent?
items.e: Rectangles (including squares) have congruent diagonals. A general rhombus does not. Rectangle.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides (its bases). Trapezoid.

items.q: Which fact is enough to prove ABCD is a parallelogram?
c: One pair of sides is parallel
items.e: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, it is a parallelogram. The diagonals bisect each other.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 4x + 6, CD = 5x − 5, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 4x + 6 = 5x − 5, so x = 11.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 5x + 4, CD = 3x + 28, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 5x + 4 = 3x + 28, so 2x = 24 and x = 12.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 3x + 8, CD = 5x, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 3x + 8 = 5x, so 2x = 8 and x = 4.

items.q: Which property does a rectangle have that a general parallelogram does not?
items.e: Every parallelogram has the other three properties. Its diagonals are congruent.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has two pairs of consecutive congruent sides but opposite sides that are not congruent?
items.e: That is the definition of a kite. Kite.
